gen-dafont-gobold-gf-hedvig-letters-seri: Hedvig Letters Serif has a sturdy, tall-bodied lowercase and curves that stay open, with ink-like modulation you can almost feel. But Gobold sits above it with wide-spaced, geometric letters of a steadier line, so a long page would read with warmth beneath a firm top.
gen-dafont-gobold-gf-marcellus-sc: Marcellus SC is a text serif with gentle modulation and pulled-back terminals, dignified and a little literary. Gobold is best at commanding, widely spaced display lines; Marcellus SC does its best work holding a quieter, cast-iron-stout line of text.
gen-dafont-gobold-gf-montagu-slab: Gobold goes wide and geometric, its curves never pinching, with short ascenders and a big lowercase. Montagu Slab brings the strongest quality of the pair: a reed-pen softness in its serif curves, sturdy downstrokes and a sizable x-height.
gen-dafont-gobold-gf-noto-serif-hentaiga: Small letters that stand almost as tall as capitals give Noto Serif Hentaigana a quietly traditional look, with subtle modulation inside each stroke. And over a long passage that gentle variation keeps things moving, while Gobold's drafting-pen line overhead stays wide and firm.
gen-dafont-gobold-gf-ovo: Curves that refuse to close, spaced far apart, make Gobold instantly recognizable as a display face. Ovo follows with a tall middle band, shallow ascenders and thins only slightly lighter than thicks, so a long read feels classic and authoritative.
gen-dafont-good-times-fs-asap: Good Times is wide, geometric and commanding, its lowercase thick as bundled cable. Asap follows with open arcs and a body height nearly matching its capitals, so a long passage reads smoothly with low contrast and a readable sans feel.
gen-dafont-good-times-fs-epilogue: Lowercase thick as bundled cable gives Good Times its weight. It does best at commanding display lines with a subtle gradient of weight along each curve, while Epilogue's wire-like monoline sans skeleton and tall body feel approachable in running text.
gen-dafont-good-times-fs-merriweather-sa: Good Times opens its e with a clear gap and keeps a slight tightening at curve tops, giving headings a geometric, commanding stance. Merriweather Sans stays low in contrast with tall, sturdy lowercase, so a long stretch of it reads large and steady.
gen-dafont-good-times-fs-public-sans: Small letters thick as bundled cable, softened by gentle contrast in every curve, make Good Times unmistakably heavy and geometric up top. Public Sans brings the strongest quality here: a hefty, trustworthy lowercase with broad open counters.
gen-dafont-good-times-fs-supreme: Heavy, wide and confident. Good Times does best at commanding display lines with moderate thick-thin modulation, while Supreme is crisp and low in contrast, holding a thick strip of text with letters kept open rather than curled shut.
